messages:
Maya: FYI ran fp4 microkernel on the 16k summarization suite — seeing consistent tail latency regressions (~10-15%) vs int8 baseline. KV cache hit rate drops by ~8% in the same window. logs: /mnt/runs/2199/fp4-run-16k.log
Trent: ugh. Was that the branch that swapped kernel tiling? which kernel impl exactly?
Maya: the new fp4_tile_v2 kernel (w/ 32x64 tiling). config: `--kernel=fp4_tile_v2 --batching=auto --kvprefetch=on`
Zhao: interesting — fp4 has smaller footprint but more frequent recompute for certain matmul paths. can you paste the perf counters?
Maya: pasted snippet from perf profiler:
```
# allocs per step
matmul_execs: 1234
kv_reads: 987
kv_misses: 78
cache_evictions: 45
avg_step_ms: 54.3 (baseline 49.1)
P50/P95/P99: 47 / 88 / 210
```

Oli: where are the evictions coming from — is it due to more KV warming because of changed cache layout?
Ben: I suspect batching heuristics interacting badly: when kernel tiling changes tokenization alignment, batch packing shifts and we get more diverse cache addresses -> fragmentation.
Priya: this matters for Dedicated customers. we should prioritize a short repro and rollback plan.
Trent: agree. quick diagnostic: can we run the same model with old kernel but fp4 quant params to separate kernel vs quant effect?
Maya: ran that: old kernel + fp4 quant -> no regression. so kernel impl + fp4 combo triggers it.
Zhao: that points to quant calibration interaction with kernel memory layout. Are we using per-channel or per-tensor scale?
Maya: per-tensor for this run (current default). calibration dataset was our standard 5k examples sampled uniformly.
Zhao: propose switching to per-channel calibration for weight matrices in attention — should reduce per-weight quant noise that causes dynamic addressing variance. but per-channel is heavier.
Oli: also noticed that long-context inputs have a skewed token-frequency distribution; uniform sampling might miss rare high-entropy tails that stress KV cache. we should stratify by sequence length & token-entropy percentile. :thinking_face:
Ben: +1. Suggest a two-pass sampler: pass1 collect seq_len, entropy hist; pass2 stratified sample with heavier weight on long/high-entropy tails. config sketch:
```
{"sampler": "two_pass",
 "pass1_size": 10000,
 "strata": ["<512","512-2048","2048-8192","8192-16384"],
 "entropy_buckets": 5,
 "weights": "inversely_proportional_to_count"
}
```

Priya: makes sense. but team debate: per-channel vs per-tensor + outlier clipping. Zhao, what about clipping extreme per-channel scales?
Zhao: clipping is necessary. my recommendation: per-channel scales with percentile-based clipping (e.g., 99.5th) and fallback to per-tensor for tiny dims. also detect 'hot' neurons and apply symmetric quantization for them.
Trent: operationally, we'll need a validation pass checking latency regressions and KV hit rate before promoting the calibration artifact. CI job idea: run 100 exemplar requests covering each stratum and collect KV stats + token-level timings.
Maya: set up a quick CI harness — I can stub a job under perf-ci/kvcache-fp4/2199.
deploy-bot: perf-regression-detect: new run 2199991111 created. baseline comparison job queued.
Oli: one more thought — our KV prefetch heuristics assume aligned chunking. kernel tiling change may need alignment shim in KV indexing to avoid fragmentation. small fix: pad cache keys to kernel-tile boundaries.
Ben: padding might also increase memory, but probably acceptable for Dedicated. we can toggle it by tier.
Priya: decision for next steps: (1) run two-pass stratified calibration dataset, (2) switch to per-channel with 99.5% clipping for attention weights, (3) run old-kernel+fp4 and new-kernel+fp4 with padding shim to isolate. owners: Maya/Zhao/Trent. deadline: EOD tomorrow.
Zhao: I'll prototype per-channel calibration + clipping and push a script: `scripts/calib/strat_cc_99p5.py`
Maya: I'll wire up the CI harness and run the four permutations.
Trent: I'll add the padding shim behind feature-flag `kv_tile_align_v2` and run microbenchmarks.
Priya: thanks all. circle back tomorrow morning with results. :thumbsup:
Ben: +1. if we get a clean fix, we should document kernel-tiling compatibility requirements in eng-ml/runbook.
Maya: ack — will add a short note to the runbook and link the artefacts.
deploy-bot: job perf-ci/kvcache-fp4/2199 finished queue. artifacts: s3://perf-artifacts/2199/.
Maya: gist with flamegraph + perf counters uploaded: https://gist.github.com/redwood/2199-fp4-kv-flame
Zhao: reading now, will post initial numbers in thread tomorrow.
Oli: appreciate the quick triage.
Maya: end of thread for now.
